paragraphs.title: The Sins of Society and Their Consequences

answers: Truth, mercy, and knowledge of God
Wealth, power, and joy
Peace, royalty, and victory
easy.explanation: Hosea says there was no truth, mercy, or knowledge of God in the land.
easy.q: What three things were absent from the land?

answers: Building cities and planting trees
Swearing, lying, killing, stealing, and committing adultery
Fasting, praying, and offering sacrifices
easy.explanation: The verse lists swearing, lying, killing, stealing, and adultery.
easy.q: Which sins are listed in verse 2?

answers: Only the priests
Only the kings of Israel
The land, its inhabitants, and the animals
easy.explanation: The land mourns, its inhabitants languish, and the beasts, birds, and fish are affected.
easy.q: Who suffers because of the condition of the land?

answers: The sins cause the land to mourn and its inhabitants to languish
The sins bring food and blessing
The sins immediately cause the people to leave the land
medium.explanation: Because of the people's wickedness, the land mourns and everyone dwelling there languishes.
medium.q: What is the connection between the people's sins and the land's condition?

answers: Blood has disappeared from the land
Acts of bloodshed have multiplied and followed one another
The people have avoided warfare
medium.explanation: The phrase portrays widespread and accumulating bloodshed.
medium.q: What does the phrase “blood toucheth blood” suggest?

answers: The animals also committed sin
The animals were chosen to rule the people
The harm done to the land affects its inhabitants and the whole natural order
medium.explanation: The mourning and wasting of the land extend to the animal world.
medium.q: Why are animals included among those affected?

answers: The only problem is a lack of information
Society has suffered both moral corruption and a broken relationship with God
The people have preserved all their important values
challenge.explanation: The verse identifies failures in truth and mercy as well as the absence of knowledge of God.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from “there is no truth, nor mercy, nor knowledge of God”?

answers: It shows how the lack of truth, mercy, and knowledge appears in actual behavior
It changes the subject to farming alone
It describes only the condition of animals
challenge.explanation: The specific crimes demonstrate the society's moral corruption.
challenge.q: How does the list of sins in verse 2 support the claim in verse 1?

answers: Knowledge of God leads to sin, and sin leads to blessing
Sins produce truth and mercy in the land
The absence of godly values produces sin, and sin brings mourning and destruction
challenge.explanation: The passage moves from missing values to multiplied crimes and then to suffering throughout the land.
challenge.q: What is the main sequence of consequences in these verses?

paragraphs.title: The Absence of Rebuke and the Rejection of Knowledge

answers: The priest
The animals
The kings of Judah
easy.explanation: The people are compared to those who strive with the priest.
easy.q: With whom are the people described as striving?

answers: The king
The prophet
The merchant
easy.explanation: The verse says that the prophet shall fall with them.

answers: The way of trade
The names of the cities
The law of their God
easy.explanation: The Lord says they have forgotten the law of their God.

answers: Rejecting knowledge causes the people and the prophet to stumble
Rejecting knowledge brings success
Rejecting knowledge prevents all correction
medium.explanation: The people fall because they reject knowledge, and the prophet falls with them.
medium.q: What is the connection between rejecting knowledge and falling?

answers: I will choose you again
I will refuse you and remove you from serving as a priest
I will send you to teach the people
medium.explanation: The Lord declares that because they rejected knowledge, He will reject them as priests.
medium.q: What does “I will also reject thee” mean in context?

answers: Everyone corrects one another
The priests correct only the kings
No man strives with or reproves another, and the people resist the priest
medium.explanation: The passage presents a society without proper rebuke and with opposition to the priest.
medium.q: How is the lack of correction described?

answers: The prophet is portrayed as part of the corrupt condition rather than separate from it
The prophet is the only animal in the land
The prophet forgot only the names of the priests
challenge.explanation: The text specifically says the prophet shall fall with the people.
challenge.q: Why does the prophet fall as well as the people?

answers: The priesthood is unrelated to knowledge
Rejecting knowledge also corrupts the office meant to preserve knowledge of God
The people receive more priests because of their ignorance
challenge.explanation: The Lord connects their rejection of knowledge with His rejection of them as priests.
challenge.q: What is the significance of the movement from rejected knowledge to rejected priesthood?

answers: The people became strong through learning
The people physically ceased to exist immediately
Lack of knowledge is presented as a central cause of the people's ruin
challenge.explanation: The verse directly connects the people's destruction with their lack of knowledge.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from “My people are destroyed for lack of knowledge”?

paragraphs.title: The Corruption of Priests and People

answers: Their glory is changed into shame
They receive praise
They become wealthy and happy
easy.explanation: The Lord says He will change their glory into shame as they sin against Him.
easy.q: What happens as the priests and people multiply their sins?

answers: The spoils of war
The sin of the people
The produce of their herds
easy.explanation: The verse says, “They eat up the sin of my people.”

answers: More hunger
More conflict
Satisfaction or increase
easy.explanation: They will eat and not have enough, and commit whoredom without increasing.
easy.q: What will not result from their sinful ways?

answers: Each will be punished according to his ways and rewarded according to his doings
Only the people will be punished
Only the priests will receive a reward
medium.explanation: The Lord says He will punish them for their ways and reward their doings.
medium.q: What repayment is promised to the people and priests?

answers: The priests refuse every offering
The priests profit from the people's sinful offerings
The people eat the law of God
medium.explanation: The phrase describes the priests' benefit from the people's sin and offerings.
medium.q: What does “They eat up the sin of my people” mean?

answers: Leaving the Lord brings abundance
There is no connection
Leaving the Lord leads to conduct that brings neither satisfaction nor blessing
medium.explanation: The passage links forsaking the Lord with eating without enough and increasing without blessing.
medium.q: What is the connection between leaving off the Lord and lacking satisfaction?

answers: They profit from sin and desire that it increase
They refuse to eat at all
They withdraw from every sacred duty
challenge.explanation: They consume the people's sin and set their hearts on their iniquity.
challenge.q: Why is the priests' sin especially serious?

answers: Only the priests are responsible
The people and priests share similar responsibility and judgment
The people receive a royal office
challenge.explanation: The comparison shows that both people and priests will answer for their conduct.
challenge.q: What does “like people, like priest” teach?

answers: The sinners multiply but become satisfied and blessed
They do not sin but are punished
They increase in sin, yet sin gives them neither satisfaction nor increase
challenge.explanation: Their sinful behavior grows, but it produces no true fulfillment or blessing.
challenge.q: How do these verses present the contradiction in sinful living?

answers: Whoredom, wine, and new wine
The law, mercy, and prayer
Work, trade, and farming
easy.explanation: The verse says that whoredom, wine, and new wine take away the heart.
easy.q: What things take away the heart?

answers: In the law of God
At their stocks and staff
From faithful priests alone
easy.explanation: The people ask counsel at their stocks, and their staff declares unto them.
easy.q: Where do the people ask for counsel?

answers: In the houses of the kings
In the centers of the cities
On the tops of mountains and upon the hills
easy.explanation: The passage mentions sacrifices on mountain tops and incense on the hills.
easy.q: Where do they sacrifice and burn incense?

answers: Counsel from stocks, a staff, and a spirit of whoredoms
Faithful teaching of the law
The leadership of righteous priests
medium.explanation: The people turn to divination and are led astray by a spirit of whoredoms.

answers: They will rejoice and rest
They will stumble because they lack understanding
They will build a new altar
medium.explanation: The statement connects a lack of understanding with falling.
medium.q: What does “the people that doth not understand shall fall” mean?

answers: There is no connection
Only the sons are affected
The people's unfaithfulness is reflected in the whoredom and adultery of daughters and spouses
medium.explanation: The passage links idolatrous unfaithfulness with sexual corruption within the family.
medium.q: How are the parents' actions connected with the condition of the family?

answers: Both are portrayed as betrayal and departure from proper faithfulness
Only family immorality is a problem
Idolatry is presented as a way to restore the family
challenge.explanation: The passage presents unfaithfulness to God and unfaithfulness within the family as related forms of corruption.
challenge.q: What is suggested by the parallel between idolatry and sexual unfaithfulness?

answers: It identifies a pleasant place where the unlawful worship occurred
It shows that the trees were the people's food source
It identifies the priests' dwelling place
challenge.explanation: The worship took place under oaks, poplars, and elms because their shadow was good.
challenge.q: Why does the passage mention the shadow of the trees?

answers: Lack of understanding leaves them vulnerable to deception and stumbling
Lack of understanding guarantees protection
Lack of understanding makes the people wiser and more independent
challenge.explanation: The verse directly connects failure to understand with falling.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the statement that the people lack understanding and therefore fall?

paragraphs.title: A Warning to Judah and Israel's Rebellion

answers: Judah
Ephraim alone
The animals
easy.explanation: Judah is warned not to offend by following Israel's example.
easy.q: Who is warned not to follow Israel's ways?

answers: Jerusalem and Hebron
Gilgal and Beth-aven
Egypt and Babylon
easy.explanation: The Lord says, “come not ye unto Gilgal, neither go ye up to Beth-aven.”
easy.q: Which places are Judah told not to visit?

answers: A gentle lamb
A mighty lion
A backsliding heifer
easy.explanation: Israel is compared to a backsliding heifer.
easy.q: What animal is Israel compared to?

answers: Not to join Israel's forbidden worship or follow its sinful example
Not to remain in the land
To join Israel in idolatry
medium.explanation: Judah is warned not to offend by copying Israel or participating in the forbidden worship.
medium.q: What is Judah commanded not to do?

answers: Faithful and obedient
Rebellious and stubborn
Weak and hungry
medium.explanation: A backsliding heifer represents one that resists direction and turns away.
medium.q: What does “backsliding” mean in the phrase “a backsliding heifer”?

answers: Rebellion leads to wandering without the protection of a settled community
Rebellion makes Israel a leader
Rebellion brings prosperity
medium.explanation: The Lord says He will let Israel wander like a lamb in a large, open place.
medium.q: What is the connection between Israel's rebellion and being fed as a lamb in a large place?

answers: To warn Judah not to learn Israel's sinful ways
To announce that Judah had already been punished
To show that Judah has no connection to the issue
challenge.explanation: The warning is intended to keep Judah from adopting Israel's practices.
challenge.q: Why is Judah warned alongside the description of Israel's sins?

answers: Oaths have no meaning
God's name should not be invoked while one's conduct contradicts His worship
Oaths are permitted only in business matters
challenge.explanation: The prohibition appears with warnings against corrupt worship and highlights the contradiction between words and conduct.
challenge.q: What does the prohibition against swearing “The LORD liveth” suggest in this context?

answers: It shows a movement from rebellion to wandering and lack of protection
It emphasizes Israel's military strength
It removes Israel's responsibility for its actions
challenge.explanation: Israel is first pictured as rebellious and then as exposed to wandering in an open place.
challenge.q: What does the image of a lamb in a large place add to the image of a backsliding heifer?

answers: A covenant with Judah
Idols
Agricultural labor
easy.explanation: The verse says, “Ephraim is joined to idols.”

answers: Honor and peace
The law and mercy
Shame
easy.explanation: The passage says that the rulers love shame.

answers: The wind
The sea
Fire
easy.explanation: The wind will bind up or carry away the kingdom in its wings.
easy.q: What will carry away the kingdom?

answers: Ephraim is attached to idols and unwilling to leave them
Ephraim is united with Judah
Ephraim is united with the priests
medium.explanation: The statement portrays Ephraim as firmly attached to idolatry.
medium.q: What does “Ephraim is joined to idols” describe?

answers: The leaders of the people
The houses and temples
The fields and wells
medium.explanation: The phrase refers to the rulers or leaders of the nation.
medium.q: What does “her rulers” refer to in the passage?

answers: The people repent and then receive blessing
Ephraim clings to idols, the wind carries away the kingdom, and the people are ashamed of their sacrifices
The people leave idols and return to the worship of the Lord
medium.explanation: The final verses move from idolatry to judgment and shame.
medium.q: What is the sequence of events at the end of the passage?

answers: Ephraim is ready to change immediately
Ephraim is persistently committed to idols, so judgment is allowed to proceed
Ephraim has been appointed to lead Judah
challenge.explanation: The command expresses the seriousness of Ephraim's continued attachment to idols.
challenge.q: What does the command “let him alone” suggest about Ephraim's condition?

answers: Their love of shame shows that they will not lead the people toward correction, and ruin follows
Shame gives the rulers new honor
The rulers' conduct has no connection with the nation's fate
challenge.explanation: The corrupt leadership contributes to the nation's movement toward judgment.
challenge.q: How is the rulers' love of shame connected with the destruction described?

answers: The sacrifices proved that idolatry had succeeded
The people will recognize that their sacrifices could not save them
The sacrifices will bring them great prosperity
challenge.explanation: The shame marks the failure and uselessness of their idolatrous sacrifices.
challenge.q: What does the people's shame because of their sacrifices mean?
